## Warm-up 🔥 {.smaller}

⏱️ 10 min

```r
gc <- c(0.55, 0.41, 0.62, 0.38, 0.71)
```

1. Print the mean
2. Print only values above 0.5
3. How many are above 0.5? (hint: `sum(gc > 0.5)`) 🤔

::: notes
0–10 min. Point 3 is a lovely R trick: TRUE counts as 1.
:::

## Reading real data 📄 {.smaller}

Remember `data/samples.csv`? Let's read it in R.

```r
seqs <- read.csv("data/samples.csv")

head(seqs)
str(seqs)        # structure: columns and their types 🔍
summary(seqs)    # min, max, mean per column 📊
nrow(seqs)
```

. . .

| R 🇷 | pandas 🐼 | Bash 🐚 |
|---|---|---|
| `read.csv("data/samples.csv")` | `pd.read_csv("data/samples.csv")` | `cat data/samples.csv` |
| `head(seqs)` | `df.head()` | `head data/samples.csv` |
| `str(seqs)` | `df.info()` / `df.dtypes` | – |
| `summary(seqs)` | `df.describe()` | – |
| `nrow(seqs)` | `len(df)` | `wc -l` (minus the header!) |

**pandas saved it with `to_csv()`. R reads it.** 🐍🤝🇷

::: notes
10–25 min. Any CSV saved by pandas with to_csv() reads straight into R — the pipeline spans two languages.
Use samples.csv from week 9 (columns: sample, organism, gc_content, length).
:::

## Missing values & saving a table 🕳️💾 {.smaller}

Real data has holes. In R a hole is **`NA`** (pandas: `NaN`)

```r
gc <- c(0.55, NA, 0.62)
mean(gc)                 # NA 😱 one hole spoils everything
mean(gc, na.rm = TRUE)   # 0.585 ✅ skip the holes
sum(is.na(gc))           # how many holes? 1
```

. . .

| R 🇷 | pandas 🐼 |
|---|---|
| `mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)` | `df["x"].mean()` (skips NaN by default) |
| `is.na(x)` | `df["x"].isna()` |
| `write.csv(seqs, "results/out.csv", row.names = FALSE)` | `df.to_csv("results/out.csv", index=False)` |

`row.names = FALSE` = `index=False`: no extra numbered column 🙅

::: notes
~5 min. The opposite default from pandas: R refuses to guess, pandas silently skips.
A CSV written by R reads straight into pandas, and the other way round.
:::

## Your first plot 📈

```r
hist(seqs$length,
     main = "Sequence length distribution",
     xlab = "Length (bp)",
     col  = "steelblue")
```

. . .

One line, and you have a figure 🎉

::: notes
The instant plot is R's best first impression. Show it live.
:::

## Three plots you will actually use {.smaller}

```r
hist(seqs$gc_content)                        # distribution 📊

plot(seqs$length, seqs$gc_content,           # relationship 🔗
     xlab = "Length", ylab = "GC",
     pch = 19, col = "darkgreen")

boxplot(gc_content ~ organism, data = seqs)  # compare groups 📦
```

. . .

| R 🇷 | matplotlib 🐍 |
|---|---|
| `hist(x)` | `plt.hist(x)` |
| `plot(x, y)` | `plt.scatter(x, y)` |
| `boxplot(y ~ group, data = df)` | `df.boxplot(column="y", by="group")` |
| `main=`, `xlab=`, `ylab=` | `plt.title()`, `plt.xlabel()`, `plt.ylabel()` |

## Saving a figure 💾

```r
png("results/gc_plot.png", width = 800, height = 600)
hist(seqs$gc_content, main = "GC content", col = "steelblue")
dev.off()          # ⚠️ don't forget this — it closes the file!
```

. . .

Python version: `plt.savefig("results/gc_plot.png")`, one line, no closing needed 🐍

Now your figure is a file you can put in a report or a thesis 📄

::: notes
25–35 min. dev.off() is the classic forgotten line — the file stays empty without it.
:::

## A word on ggplot2 🎨 {.smaller}

```r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(seqs, aes(x = length, y = gc_content)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "GC vs length")
```

. . .

Prettier, more powerful, and a whole language of its own.
Base R plots are enough for today: ggplot2 gets **its own block** next class 🌱

::: notes
Teaser only, Week 12 Block 2 is the full ggplot2 block.
:::

## Exercise: Analyse your own data 🧬 {.smaller}

⏱️ 30 min · breakout rooms · switch after 15 min

Create `scripts/plot_report.R`:

1. Pick a CSV: `data/samples.csv` or a CSV from **your project** 🐍
2. Read it into R with `read.csv()`
3. Print `summary()` and the number of rows
4. Make a histogram of lengths 📊
5. Make a scatter plot of two numeric columns 🔗
6. Save one figure into `results/` and commit the **script** (not the PNG 🙈)

💡 **Bonus:** recreate one of your project plots in R 🇷

::: notes
35–75 min. Most common failure: wrong working directory (setwd / RStudio project). Have samples.csv in the chat as plan B.
:::

## Wrap-up ✅ {.smaller}

| R 🇷 | Python 🐍 |
|---|---|
| `read.csv()` | `pd.read_csv()` 📄 |
| `summary()` / `str()` | `describe()` / `info()` 🔍 |
| `hist()` `plot()` `boxplot()` | `plt.hist()` `plt.scatter()` `boxplot()` 📊 |
| `png()` … `dev.off()` | `plt.savefig()` 💾 |

**Commit** 💾 your R script.
